claims.text: HPHT treatment followed by controlled cooling can induce a hierarchical microstructure in a eutectic HEA.
The induced microstructure will contain a continuous, ductile BCC matrix reinforced by coherent fine-scale δ lamellae and γ″ particles.
The engineered microstructure will simultaneously enhance yield strength and tensile ductility relative to the untreated alloy.
The engineered microstructure will increase Young's modulus relative to the untreated alloy.
The engineered microstructure will improve fracture resistance relative to the untreated alloy.
An as-cast or homogenized eutectic HEA generally has a mixed soft FCC/BCC or weakly ordered microstructure without optimized phase distribution.
Treatment at approximately 6 GPa and elevated temperature for a couple of hours, followed by rapid cooling, will trigger controlled phase transformation and coherent precipitation.
Property improvement requires a low, uniformly dispersed precipitate volume fraction of roughly a few percent.
Formation of a continuous brittle second phase or loss of interface coherency will prevent the proposed property improvement.
Coherent δ lamellae and γ″ precipitates pin dislocations.
Coherent δ lamellae and γ″ precipitates deflect cleavage cracks.
HPHT treatment refines grains and alters phase stability so as to promote controlled precipitate nucleation.
The precipitates enhance work hardening by impeding dislocation motion.
A ductile continuous matrix preserves sufficient plasticity while the precipitates provide strengthening.
Crack deflection and blunting by the engineered microstructure improve fracture resistance.
The HPHT-treated alloy may achieve approximately twice the yield and ultimate tensile strengths of the untreated alloy.
The HPHT-treated alloy may exhibit a 1.5- to 2-fold increase in tensile ductility.
The HPHT-treated alloy will exhibit a moderate increase in Young's modulus.
The HPHT-treated alloy will exhibit lower crack-propagation rates and greater fracture-energy absorption.
Extremely high or uncontrolled pressure and temperature can generate microcracks or deleterious segregation.
